name: HOUSE OF CARDS
description: House of Cards is a dual-purpose term. While it commonly refers to the physical act of building towers with playing cards, it is also a specific, traditional drawing and building game. In its game form, players compete to build virtual 'rooms' and 'stories' by matching colors and ranks to score points based on triangle formations.

content.text: House of Cards is a dual-purpose term. While it commonly refers to the physical act of building towers with playing cards, it is also a specific, traditional drawing and building game. In its game form, players compete to build virtual 'rooms' and 'stories' by matching colors and ranks to score points based on triangle formations.
Derived from architectural parlor games of the 18th century, where cards were used as visual aids or components for geometric challenges.
Two players. Each player is assigned a color (Red or Black) in the common half-deck variant; with the full deck both take turns placing cards to build the shared house structure.
Standard 52-card deck. Often split by color (Red vs Black).

Players draw cards to their hand (usually 3 at a time) to build their 'house'.

items.text: Half deck: Use 26 cards (e.g. Red vs Black); each player is assigned a color.
Collapse variant: A player may force a collapse when unable to win; the opponent who last placed a card incurs a penalty.
Other variants: House rules may vary initial deal size, scoring of ties, or number of cards per draw.
